findings.title: Contract is silent on several request edge cases the backend now fixes implicitly (mux redirects, duplicate keys, underflow, Content-Type leniency)
findings.evidence: Verified 2026-10-13. (1) Coordinator smoke on :8080: GET /api -> 307 Temporary Redirect, Location: /api/, text/html body; GET /api/ -> 404 problem+json NOT_FOUND. openapi.yaml line 45 only defines 404 NOT_FOUND for 'No route under /api/'. Reviewer probes (httptest, run by the review worker): POST //api/v1/calculations, /api/v1/./calculations and /api/x/../v1/calculations -> 307 with empty body (net/http ServeMux path cleaning). (2) Reviewer probes: duplicate keys, last wins ({"operation":"add","operation":"subtract","operands":[5,3]} -> 200 subtract = 2); operand 1e-400 underflows to 0, so divide [1,1e-400] -> 422 DIVISION_BY_ZERO; Content-Type 'application/json;', 'charset="utf-8"', a trailing tab and a repeated identical charset are accepted by mime.ParseMediaType.
findings.impact: Low: none of these affect valid calculations or the frontend; clients hitting them get a redirect or a lenient interpretation the contract does not document.
findings.precautions: Decide in a contract branch (docs/api is read-only for backend/frontend branches): document the current behavior or tighten it with examples; then align httpapi (e.g. an exact '/api' route) in a backend branch.

snapshot.title: Contract is silent about /api without a trailing slash (Go mux answers 307 HTML redirect)
snapshot.evidence: Verified on 2026-10-13 against the built server on :8080: GET /api -> 307 Temporary Redirect, Location: /api/, Content-Type text/html; charset=utf-8, body 'Temporary Redirect.'; GET /api/ -> 404 application/problem+json NOT_FOUND. openapi.yaml line 45 only defines 404 NOT_FOUND for 'No route under /api/'. The redirect comes from net/http ServeMux subtree handling of the '/api/' pattern in backend/internal/httpapi/routes.go.
snapshot.impact: Low: a client calling /api gets an HTML redirect instead of a problem document; no calculation path is affected and the frontend never calls /api.
snapshot.precautions: Decide in a contract branch (docs/api is read-only for backend/frontend branches): either document that /api redirects to /api/, or require a 404 problem for /api and add an example; then register an exact '/api' route in httpapi.

findings.title: No project license chosen; OpenAPI info.license missing
findings.evidence: Forge check openapi-lint (receipt d32cebdd-aa5b-4ae1-9b25-f9dc55f5b7f7) reports warning info-license at docs/api/openapi.yaml:2:1. The repository has no LICENSE file; docs/spec.md lists the license as an open question.
findings.impact: Reviewers and reusers cannot tell under which terms the project code may be used; the contract lint keeps one warning.
findings.precautions: Only the repository owner chooses a license. Vendored skills keep their own MIT notices regardless of the project license.
findings.verification: After a license is chosen: add LICENSE, set info.license in openapi.yaml and rerun npx --yes @redocly/cli@2.54.2 lint docs/api/openapi.yaml.

findings.title: sqrt-negative example and openapi.yaml show a detail text the server never returns
findings.evidence: Verified 2026-10-14 by the task 4 E2E smoke (curl direct on :8080 and through the Vite proxy on :5173) replaying docs/api/examples/sqrt-negative.json: the server returns 422 DOMAIN_ERROR with detail "The operation is undefined for these operands." while the example and openapi.yaml (line 331) show "Square root of a negative number is undefined.". Status, content type, code and every other member match. backend/internal/httpapi/contract_test.go only requires detail to be non-empty, and openapi.yaml says detail is not part of the contract, so no test fails. Task 2 kept a generic DOMAIN_ERROR detail on purpose (review nit left as is).
findings.impact: Low: clients branch on code only; a reader comparing the README or the examples with real responses sees a different sentence for this one case.
findings.precautions: docs/api is changed only in its own contract branch. Either align the example and openapi.yaml with the generic detail, or make the backend detail operation-specific in a backend branch; do not patch one side alone.
findings.verification: After the fix, the task 4 E2E comparison reports no detail differences for the 17 examples.

findings.title: frontend/package.json engines (>=22.12) is looser than the dev toolchain requires (jsdom: ^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26)
findings.evidence: Verified 2026-10-14: npm ci on Node v24.14.0 / npm 11.9.0 prints EBADENGINE for jsdom@30.1.2, @asamuzakjp/css-color@7.1.5, @asamuzakjp/dom-selector@9.2.4 and w3c-xmlserializer@6.0.0, each requiring node '^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0'; frontend/package.json declares "engines": { "node": ">=22.12" }. All checks still pass on 24.14.0 (lint, typecheck, 187 tests, build). CI and the Dockerfile pin Node 24.21.0, which satisfies the range.
findings.impact: Low: a contributor on Node 22.12-22.22.1 or 24.0-24.14 gets warnings and possibly test-tooling failures that the declared engines range says should not happen. Runtime and build output are unaffected.
findings.precautions: Changing engines is a frontend change for a frontend branch; the READMEs already state the real range. Do not add engine-strict without checking the CI and Docker Node versions.
findings.verification: Set engines.node to '^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26' (or the range the toolchain then requires) and run npm ci on the minimum version without EBADENGINE warnings.

findings.title: iOS decimal keypad may block negative numbers and comma-locale input
findings.evidence: Suspected, not verified on a device: inputMode="decimal" (required by ADR 0005 and the task) shows the iOS decimal pad, which has no minus key, and in comma-decimal locales it offers ',' which parseOperand rejects by design. Reported by the task 3 reviewer from platform knowledge; no iPhone was available.
findings.impact: Some iPhone users may be unable to type negative operands or decimals with the on-screen keypad.
findings.precautions: Verify on a real iOS device before changing anything; inputMode and the dot-only rule are spec decisions (ADR 0005, spec feature 4), so a change needs a spec or ADR update first.

findings.title: Percentage overflow fallback can report RESULT_OUT_OF_RANGE for a result that rounds to MaxFloat64
findings.evidence: Verified 2026-10-13 with a scratch probe (.forge/tmp/backend-api/probe): a=2.632632520997171e+287, b=6.82850006799049e+22; a*b/100 = +Inf and the fallback a/100*b = +Inf, while the exact value (big.Float, 200 bits) is 1.797693134862315679e+308 <= MaxFloat64 1.7976931348623157e+308. The review worker's random search found 161 of 146,719 fallback cases within 1e-15 below MaxFloat64 behaving this way. The code follows the contract's formula ((a/100)*b fallback) literally.
findings.impact: Negligible in practice: only results within ~1 ulp of MaxFloat64 are affected; they return 422 instead of MaxFloat64.
findings.precautions: Only fix together with a contract note: e.g. scale with math.Frexp/Ldexp, and add the probe case to TestCalculate. Keep the fuzz invariant (never NaN/Inf with nil error).

findings.title: Result panel can render below the fold on short phones after Calculate
findings.evidence: Verified by the task 3 reviewer in Chrome mobile emulation: at 360x640 and 390x664 the Calculate button bottom is y=627 and the result panel starts at y=668, outside the viewport; nothing scrolls it into view. At 360x740 and 412x800 it is fully visible. Screen reader users get the result through the role=status live region.
findings.impact: Sighted touch users on short screens see no outcome until they scroll.
findings.precautions: A fix such as scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' }) on status change needs a jsdom stub in src/test/setup.ts and must respect prefers-reduced-motion; do not move focus to the result.

findings.title: Go 1.27.0 toolchain: 6 reachable net/http standard library vulnerabilities fixed in Go 1.27.2
findings.evidence: Verified: govulncheck on backend/ with go1.27.0 (saved in .forge/tmp/delivery/review/govulncheck.txt) reports 6 vulnerabilities reachable from our code, all fixed in go1.27.2: GO-2026-6617 (HTTP/2 HPACK encoder race, server crash), GO-2026-6613 (HTTP/1 desync after 2xx CONNECT), GO-2026-6612 (HTTP/2 double flow-control refund), GO-2026-6611 (CPU from repeated HTTP/2 initial window changes), GO-2026-6609 (no limit on parsed Range headers, reached through http.FileServer in internal/httpapi/routes.go), GO-2026-6603 (HTTP/2 memory exhaustion via Trailer headers). Traces go through cmd/server/main.go (http.Server.Serve/Shutdown) and internal/httpapi (middleware, routes). go.mod declared go 1.27.0 and the Dockerfile built with golang:1.27.0-bookworm.
findings.impact: The shipped binary (Docker image and local builds) was exposed to denial of service (crash, CPU and memory exhaustion) and HTTP/1 desynchronization from untrusted clients.
findings.precautions: Keep go.mod and the Dockerfile builder on the same patch release; rerun govulncheck (golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck) before each release, since new standard library advisories appear often.
findings.verification: 2026-10-14: backend/go.mod raised to go 1.27.2 and the Dockerfile to golang:1.27.2-bookworm. go version in backend/ reports go1.27.2; govulncheck v1.8.0 ./... prints 'No vulnerabilities found.' (.forge/tmp/delivery/review/govulncheck-1.27.2.txt); go test passes (calculator 100 %, httpapi 95.4 %).

findings.title: Static SPA serving has no Cache-Control for hashed assets and no compression
findings.evidence: Suspected (code reading in the task 4 review, not measured): STATIC_DIR is served with http.FileServer behind noListing; no Cache-Control header is set, so the content-hashed files in /assets/ are revalidated instead of cached as immutable, and responses are not gzip/brotli compressed. No load test or Lighthouse run was done.
findings.impact: Slower repeat and first loads over slow networks; negligible for a local assessment demo with one small bundle.
findings.precautions: Measure first. If needed, add Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable only for /assets/*, keep index.html no-cache, and prefer precompressed files or a reverse proxy over a third-party module (standard library only).
